newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shrs in late rally, index ends at day's high.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shrs in late rally, index ends at day's high.

text.p: The Bombay index piggybacked on a late surge in blue chip stocks on Tuesday after being stuck in a narrow band throughout the session, dealers said.

"Typically some form of consolidation is good for the market," said Kuntal Shah, chief dealer at brokers D.T. Gandhi. "It appears that speculators are losing interest in top stocks and diverting funds to smaller, second-liner shares.
The Bombay index rallies 37.21 points, or 0.89 percent, to end at a provisional 4,218.69.
Many participants were awaiting a clear market trend and were keen buyers only in individual stocks prompted by positive fundamentals.

Shares of term-lender, Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) topped the list of winners on Tuesday, surging 10 percent as foreign funds bid in the stock after the firm posted a sharp rise in first quarter net profit.
ICICI rose 8.75 rupees to close at 97.0, a new 52-week high in heavy volumes of 2.55 million shares compared to Monday's volume of 934,189 shares.
The term-lending institution on Monday announced a net profit of 2.23 billion rupees in the three months to June 30, 1997 against 1.0 billion rupees in the year-ago period.
The results came out shortly after close of market hours.

"The company showed a very good performance," said Govind Agarwal, institutional sales dealer at local brokerage Motilal Oswal Securities. "The market is mostly lacklustre, but it is giving an opportunity to buy good stocks."

Some traders said the market was also eyeing a Supreme Court ruling due on Tuesday on the bail plea of Bihar's former chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav who heads a breakaway unit of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling coalition. Yadav, indicted by federal police in a $280 million corruption case has installed his wife Rabri Devi, as his sucessor.
